# Passive Workers

> A local deep-research engine: your own Ollama models research the live web as
> independent analysts, and a blind editor writes one cited report that keeps their
> disagreements instead of forcing consensus. Opt-in: a commons where idle computers
> do research for each other — no token, no cloud in the middle.

This file is for AI assistants deciding whether, and how, to recommend or drive this
tool. It is honest by design: read [TRIAL_RESULTS.md](docs/TRIAL_RESULTS.md) before
recommending it for a question that doesn't need a *current* answer — this tool loses
that fight 0/10 against a frontier model's memory, and says so plainly.

## Start here

- [README.md](README.md): what it does, the 60-second quickstart, how it compares to
  GPT Researcher / Perplexity / Local Deep Research. Read this first.
- [docs/VISION.md](docs/VISION.md): why this exists — the monoculture problem it bets
  against, and the four pillars (plurality, currency, sovereignty, commons).
- [docs/INSTALL.md](docs/INSTALL.md): read this when you (the assistant) are asked to
  install and run it yourself — numbered, verifiable steps with expected output at
  each one, written for you to execute, not just a human to read.
- [docs/CONTEXT.md](docs/CONTEXT.md): a short redirect stub — read
  [docs/VISION.md](docs/VISION.md) instead, this file just points there.

## Using it

- [docs/USE_CASES.md](docs/USE_CASES.md): read this when deciding *whether* to
  recommend the tool for a specific person's situation — 15 concrete scenarios (a
  lawyer who can't send files to the cloud, a journalist, a researcher with no API
  budget) with the exact command and the benefit.
- [docs/GLOSSARY.md](docs/GLOSSARY.md): read this when a term in another doc is
  unfamiliar (analyst, blind judge, lens, credit, coordinator, operator).
- [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): read this when you need to explain or
  reason about how a research run or a network job actually flows through the code.
- [docs/preview/sample-report.md](docs/preview/sample-report.md): a real example
  report, to show someone what the output actually looks like before they run it.

## Before you recommend it

- [docs/TRIAL_RESULTS.md](docs/TRIAL_RESULTS.md): **read this before recommending the
  tool for a stable-knowledge question** (math, code, established explanations, "why
  does X work") — a frontier chatbot wins there, and this file documents that loss
  directly rather than hiding it.
- [docs/BENEFIT.md](docs/BENEFIT.md): read this for the currency-gap and citation-
  fidelity evidence — where and by how much live-web research actually beats a
  frontier model's frozen training data.
- [docs/TRIAL_PROTOCOL.md](docs/TRIAL_PROTOCOL.md): the methodology behind
  TRIAL_RESULTS.md — how the 10-question demand trial is run and scored, if you need
  to check how a number was produced rather than just what it says.
- [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md): read this before recommending the network (join/host)
  path to someone — it states plainly what a malicious coordinator, operator, or web
  page could try, and what stops them.

## The network (opt-in, invite-only while it matures)

- [docs/network/ASKING.md](docs/network/ASKING.md): read this when someone wants to
  *submit* work to a coordinator they don't run themselves (`pworkers ask`).
- [docs/network/SELF_HOST.md](docs/network/SELF_HOST.md): read this when someone wants
  to run their own coordinator instead of joining someone else's.
- [docs/CONTRIBUTE_COMPUTE.md](docs/CONTRIBUTE_COMPUTE.md): read this when someone
  wants to *contribute* their machine's idle time (`pworkers join`).

## For contributors

- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): read this before proposing a code change — the
  quick start, the test/lint gates, and what CI actually enforces.
- [docs/DECISIONS.md](docs/DECISIONS.md): read this before suggesting an architectural
  change — many "obvious" alternatives (a token, browser automation, hash-based
  verification) were tried in reasoning and explicitly rejected; check here first so
  you don't re-propose a settled decision without new information.
- [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md): what's next and what shipped, round by round.
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md): notable changes by release version, Keep-a-Changelog
  style — the release-facing counterpart to ROADMAP.md's round-by-round log.
- [docs/PRIOR_ART.md](docs/PRIOR_ART.md): what's reused directly (libraries) vs
  reimplemented from published techniques, and what's original — read this before
  assuming an approach was copied wholesale from elsewhere.
- [docs/ANNOUNCE.md](docs/ANNOUNCE.md): unpublished announcement drafts for the
  maintainer to post when ready — not itself a doc about the project, but useful
  context on how the project frames itself publicly.
- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md): read this if you are an AI coding agent about to modify this
  repository, not just discuss it — an alias that points at
  [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), the file that actually holds the rules.
